prerequisites: Good knowledge of the basic concepts of linear algebra and of real and complex analysis.

Ability to apply methods learned during first year exams: graphs of elementary functions, computation of derivatives and integrals, operations with complex numbers, matrix and vector arithmetic, computation of eigenvalues.
Attendance and passing of examinations for "Analisi Matematica 1", "Fisica 1", and "Geometry and Algebra" courses.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire a working knowledge of the fundamental methodologies of linear algebra and Fourier analysis, as well as the basic methods for the numerical solution of ordinary differential equations, with rigorous theoretical justification.
Apply the treated methods for the solution of other mathematical problems, mainly differential ones, and for the resolution of applicative problems typical of engineering branches.
Apply the methodologies described in the course to the solution of problems encountered in their own field of interest.
Identify the most important theoretical properties for a particular problem.
Choose the most suitable algorithm for problem solution.
Communicate knowledge and understanding methodically and consistently, as evaluated in written and optional oral tests.
Acquire a basic expertise sufficient to understand advanced mathematical texts for widening their knowledge autonomously.

syllabus_topics: Numerical linear algebra: Review of linear algebra
Solution of linear systems by means of direct methods (Gaussian elimination)
Solution of linear systems by means of iterative methods (Jacobi and Gauss Seidel)
Applied Fourier analysis: Periodic functions and trigonometric polynomials
Periodic extension of a function and Fourier series
Ordinary Differential Equations: Formulation of Cauchy problems
Existence and uniqueness of the solution
Systems of differential equations of the first order and equations of order larger than one
Local discretization error for multistep methods
assessment_rules: Grading consists of a written test, usually five exercises, completed in three hours. To pass, a grade of at least 18/30 is required. An optional oral interview can be requested by the student or the teacher to improve or correctly evaluate the final grade. An alternative grading mode involves two written tests, each requiring a minimum of 18/30, with a final oral interview also possible.
